q-66873.name: Question 1
q-66873.problem: Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${10}^{x-2}={3}^{x}?$
q-66873.worked_solution:
First, we take the common logarithm $(log)$ of both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x-2} & ={3}^{x} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x-2}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({3}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x-2=\operatorname{log}⁡({3}^{x})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x-2=x\operatorname{log}⁡(3)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(3) \\ x-x\operatorname{log}⁡(3) & =2 \\ x(1-\operatorname{log}⁡(3)) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{1-\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of x satisfies the equation 10x−2=3x?

a
21−log⁡(3)
b
1+log⁡(3)
c
−3log⁡(2)
d
12−log⁡(3)
e
log⁡(2)+log⁡(3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we take the common logarithm (log) of both sides of the equation: 10x−2=3xlog⁡(10x−2)=log⁡(3x)

Now, we use the fact that logb⁡(bc)=c to simplify the left-hand side. This gives: x−2=log⁡(3x)

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side: x−2=xlog⁡(3)

Finally, we solve for x, as follows: x−2=xlog⁡(3)x−xlog⁡(3)=2x(1−log⁡(3))=2x=21−log⁡(3)

q-242900.name: Question 2
q-242900.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{5}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x+4} & ={2}^{2-x} \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{x+4}) & ={log}_{5}⁡({2}^{2-x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
x+4={log}_{5}⁡({2}^{2-x})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+4=(2-x){log}_{5}⁡(2)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+4 & =(2-x){log}_{5}⁡(2) \\ x+4 & =2{log}_{5}⁡(2)-x{log}_{5}⁡(2) \\ x+x{log}_{5}⁡(2) & =2{log}_{5}⁡(2)-4 \\ x(1+{log}_{5}⁡(2)) & =2{log}_{5}⁡(2)-4 \\ x & =\frac{2{log}_{5}⁡(2)-4}{1+{log}_{5}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{5}⁡(2)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}≈0.430\,677.
$$

Finally, we can approximate $x$ as

$$
x≈\frac{2\cdot 0.430\,677-4}{1+0.430\,677}≈-2.194,
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

q-26828.name: Question 3
q-26828.problem: Given that ${5}^{y}={4}^{y+1},$ what is the value of $y?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
q-26828.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{5}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{y}={4}^{y+1} \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{y}) & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =y{log}_{5}⁡4+{log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y-y{log}_{5}⁡4 & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y(1-{log}_{5}⁡4) & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =\frac{{log}_{5}⁡4}{1-{log}_{5}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{5}⁡(4)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}≈0.861\,353.
$$

Finally, then, we can approximate $y$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}y≈\frac{0.861\,353}{1-0.861\,353}≈6.213,\end{aligned}
$$

to $3$ decimal places.

Given that 5y=4y+1, what is the value of y? Round your answer to 3 decimal places.

a
6.213
b
−5.891

First, we take log5 on both sides of the equation:

5y=4y+1log5⁡(5y)=log5⁡(4y+1)

Now, we use the fact that logb⁡(bc)=c to simplify the left-hand side:

y=log5⁡(4y+1)

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

y=(y+1)log5⁡4

Finally, we solve for y, as follows:

y=(y+1)log5⁡4y=ylog5⁡4+log5⁡4y−ylog5⁡4=log5⁡4y(1−log5⁡4)=log5⁡4y=log5⁡41−log5⁡4

Using the change of base formula, we have

log5⁡(4)=ln⁡(4)ln⁡(5)≈0.861353.

Finally, then, we can approximate y as

y≈0.8613531−0.861353≈6.213, to 3 decimal places.

q-26830.name: Question 4
q-26830.problem: Given that $\frac{{3}^{x}}{5}=3\cdot {4}^{x},$ what is the value of $x?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
q-26830.worked_solution:
First, notice that, by multiplying by $5$ on both sides,  the given equation is equivalent to

$$
{3}^{x}=15\cdot {4}^{x}
$$

Now, we take ${log}_{3}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
{log}_{3}⁡({3}^{x})={log}_{3}⁡(15\cdot {4}^{x})
$$

Then, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{3}⁡(15\cdot {4}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use  the product law and the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{3}⁡(15\cdot {4}^{x}) \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(15)+{log}_{3}⁡({4}^{x}) \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(15)+x{log}_{3}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{3}⁡(15)+x{log}_{3}⁡4 \\ x-x{log}_{3}⁡4 & ={log}_{3}⁡(15) \\ x(1-{log}_{3}⁡4) & ={log}_{3}⁡(15) \\ x & =\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(15)}{1-{log}_{3}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{3}⁡(15)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡15}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}≈2.464\,974, \\ {log}_{3}⁡4=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}≈1.261\,860.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can approximate $x$ as

$$
x≈\frac{2.464\,974}{1-1.261\,860}≈-9.413,
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

First, notice that, by multiplying by 5 on both sides, the given equation is equivalent to 3x=15⋅4x

Now, we take log3 on both sides of the equation:

log3⁡(3x)=log3⁡(15⋅4x)

Then, we use the fact that logb⁡(bc)=c to simplify the left-hand side:

x=log3⁡(15⋅4x)

Next, we use the product law and the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

x=log3⁡(15⋅4x)=log3⁡(15)+log3⁡(4x)=log3⁡(15)+xlog3⁡4

Finally, we solve for x, as follows:

x=log3⁡(15)+xlog3⁡4x−xlog3⁡4=log3⁡(15)x(1−log3⁡4)=log3⁡(15)x=log3⁡(15)1−log3⁡4

Using the change of base formula, we have log3⁡(15)=ln⁡15ln⁡3≈2.464974,log3⁡4=ln⁡4ln⁡3≈1.261860.

Finally, we can approximate x as x≈2.4649741−1.261860≈−9.413, rounded to 3 decimal places.

q-66883.problem: Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${10}^{x+1}={3}^{x+2}?$
q-66883.worked_solution:
First, we take the common logarithm $(log)$ of both sides of the equation:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x+1} & ={3}^{x+2} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x+1}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({3}^{x+2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1=\operatorname{log}⁡({3}^{x+2})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =(x+2)\operatorname{log}⁡(3) \\ x+1 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{log}⁡(3) \\ x-x\operatorname{log}⁡(3) & =2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)-1 \\ x(1-\operatorname{log}⁡(3)) & =2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)-1 \\ x & =\frac{2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)-1}{1-\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{3x-1} & ={9}^{x+6} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{3x-1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{x+6})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(3x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)=(x+6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =(x+6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)+6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x+3} & ={2}^{5-4x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{5-4x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(5-4x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(6x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)=(x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(6x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)+7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x(6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x & =\frac{7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}\end{aligned}
$$
